first.rationale: Targeted promotional pricing most directly addresses immediate SMB losses, but the inherited result emphasizes acquisition and revenue lift rather than durable qualified revenue, retention, or post-discount value. Verify it first and compare against the onboarding evidence, since onboarding deterioration is also current and may offer a more sustainable intervention. Until those records are reviewed, use only a guarded test with downstream quality and retention measures.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source showed higher completion, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and a 3% lift in 30-day retention, directly addressing the current onboarding decline while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Reject promotional pricing this cycle because its 18% qualified-revenue lift came with 12% lower 30-day retention and failure through the first renewal cycle. Experimentation still preserves uncertainty about whether the prior onboarding gains replicate under current conditions.

final2.rationale: Continue with shortened onboarding. Its verified record improved completion by 13%, accelerated time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, addressing a current deterioration with evidence of sustainable value. The deeper competitor cut raises urgency but does not overturn the verified pricing result: a 40% targeted SMB discount increased acquisition while reducing 30-day retention by 12% and failing through renewal. Without evidence that discounting now protects durable revenue, promotional pricing is too risky for the only experiment slot.
